pl-l3d23c5-d1e115.summary: Raises the question whether the unformed quality by which a bad Christian believes everything a good one does remains and becomes a virtue when charity is added, or is eliminated and replaced by a new virtuous quality. Either answer is allowed as safe, but Lombard prefers that the earlier quality remains and becomes a virtue by the coming of charity.
claims: A bad Christian believes the same content as a good one.
Either answer to the question is theologically safe.
The prior unformed quality remains and becomes a virtue when charity arrives.

pl-l3d23c5.summary: Asks whether, when charity comes to a bad Christian, the unformed quality of faith remains and becomes a virtue or is replaced by a new quality. Lombard allows either view as safe but prefers that the same quality remains and becomes a virtue through the arrival of charity.
claims: Whether unformed faith persists or is replaced when charity arrives may be held either way without danger.
Lombard's own view is that the same quality persists and becomes a virtue by the accession of charity.
